raw.description: Elections delivered a fragmented parliament with no party able to form a government, elevating the risk of a disorderly Greek exit from the euro and forcing a re-run vote.
raw.middle_circle: Markets had priced elevated political risk; the failure of mainstream parties to secure a majority exceeded the more optimistic scenarios of a quick pro-bailout coalition.
raw.outer_circle: Athens stock market plunged as much as 8%; euro weakened; peripheral yields rose; global risk assets sold off on renewed Grexit fears.
raw.notes: First of two 2012 Greek elections; second held on 17 June.

raw.title: JPMorgan discloses multi-billion-dollar London Whale trading losses
raw.description: JPMorgan Chase revealed more than $2 billion in losses (later revised higher to over $6 billion) from complex credit-derivative positions taken by its Chief Investment Office in London, known as the “London Whale” trades.
raw.middle_circle: The bank had previously downplayed media reports of large positions; the scale of the loss and subsequent restatement surprised investors and regulators.
raw.outer_circle: JPM shares fell sharply (over 9% the next day); financial sector underperformed; the episode intensified debate over the Volcker Rule and bank proprietary trading.
raw.notes: Initial disclosure on 10 May; losses later revised substantially higher.

raw.title: Facebook completes $16 billion IPO
raw.description: Facebook priced its IPO at $38 per share, valuing the company at approximately $104 billion, and began trading on Nasdaq amid technical glitches and heavy volume. The stock closed near the offer price after an initial pop.
raw.middle_circle: High expectations for a strong debut given the company’s profile; many anticipated a significant first-day premium, though some warned of valuation and supply concerns after the deal size was increased.
raw.outer_circle: Shares opened above $40 then faded to close near $38; related social and tech names sold off; the flat debut and subsequent decline cooled the IPO market for other tech issuers.
raw.notes: Nasdaq experienced order-matching delays; underwriters supported the stock near the offer price.

raw.title: Spain requests up to €100 billion bank bailout
raw.description: The Spanish government formally requested European financial assistance of up to €100 billion to recapitalise its banking sector after stress tests revealed large capital shortfalls, particularly at savings banks.
raw.middle_circle: Markets expected some form of bank support; the size of the envelope was large, but concerns persisted that the aid would increase sovereign debt and that conditionality details remained unclear.
raw.outer_circle: Initial relief rally in Spanish assets and the euro quickly faded; Spanish and Italian yields rose again; equities gave back early gains as investors questioned the programme’s design.
raw.notes: Request announced over the weekend of 9–10 June; market reaction on Monday 11 June was notably weak.

raw.title: Pro-bailout parties win Greek re-run election
raw.description: New Democracy and other parties supporting the international bailout programme secured enough seats to form a coalition, reducing the immediate risk of a Greek exit from the euro.
raw.middle_circle: Markets had hoped for a pro-bailout outcome; the narrow victory was welcomed but many analysts warned that fundamental problems and implementation risks remained unresolved.
raw.outer_circle: Initial relief rally in equities and the euro; Greek bank stocks surged; gains proved short-lived as attention returned to Spain and Italy.
raw.notes: Second election after the inconclusive May vote.

raw.title: Eurozone summit agrees direct bank recapitalisation and growth measures
raw.description: Leaders agreed that the permanent bailout fund could eventually inject capital directly into banks (breaking the sovereign-bank loop) and endorsed a €120 billion growth package, while relaxing some conditions on Spain’s bank aid.
raw.middle_circle: Markets expected limited progress; the agreement on direct bank recapitalisation exceeded many forecasts and was viewed as a step toward banking union.
raw.outer_circle: Equities and the euro rallied strongly; peripheral yields fell; the positive reaction was more sustained than after previous summits.
raw.notes: Summit concluded in the early hours of 29 June.

raw.title: JPMorgan revises London Whale losses higher and restates earnings
raw.description: JPMorgan announced that London Whale-related losses had reached approximately $5.8 billion for the first half and restated first-quarter results, acknowledging valuation and control failures.
raw.middle_circle: Further upward revisions to the loss estimate had been anticipated after the initial May disclosure; the restatement still damaged management credibility.
raw.outer_circle: JPM shares remained under pressure; the episode continued to weigh on bank-sector sentiment and regulatory discussions.
raw.notes: Follow-on disclosure to the May announcement.

raw.title: Spanish 10-year yields approach euro-era highs amid banking stress
raw.description: Spanish borrowing costs remained under intense pressure, with 10-year yields trading near levels that had previously forced other countries into full sovereign programmes, highlighting the sovereign-bank feedback loop.
raw.middle_circle: After the June bank bailout request, markets still demanded clearer conditionality and a stronger European backstop before yields could sustainably decline.
raw.outer_circle: Yields remained elevated until Draghi’s late-July intervention; equity and bank stocks stayed under pressure.
raw.notes: Context for the subsequent Draghi speech.

raw.title: Mario Draghi declares ECB ready to do 'whatever it takes' to preserve the euro
raw.description: In a speech in London, ECB President Mario Draghi stated that the central bank was ready to do whatever it takes to preserve the euro within its mandate, adding “believe me, it will be enough.”
raw.middle_circle: Markets had grown sceptical of verbal interventions; few expected such a clear and forceful commitment that would later be backed by the OMT programme.
raw.outer_circle: Euro surged; Spanish and Italian yields dropped sharply (10-year Spanish yield fell below 7%); European and global equities rallied strongly in a multi-day risk-on move.
raw.notes: Widely regarded as a turning point in the eurozone crisis; set the stage for the September OMT announcement.

raw.title: ECB leaves policy unchanged but signals possible bond-market action
raw.description: At its August meeting the ECB kept rates steady while Draghi indicated that the Governing Council would work on modalities for intervening in bond markets to address severe distortions, building on his late-July speech.
raw.middle_circle: Markets expected further clarification after the “whatever it takes” remarks; the absence of immediate action was balanced by clearer signalling of forthcoming measures.
raw.outer_circle: Peripheral yields continued to ease from July extremes; risk assets remained supported ahead of the September OMT decision.
raw.notes: Interim step between the July speech and the September OMT announcement.

raw.title: ECB announces Outright Monetary Transactions (OMT) programme
raw.description: The ECB unveiled an unlimited secondary-market government bond purchase programme (OMT) for countries under an ESM programme with strict conditionality, aimed at removing “unfounded” risk premia and restoring monetary-policy transmission.
raw.middle_circle: After Draghi’s July speech, markets expected a bond-buying framework; the unlimited nature and conditionality details were broadly in line with, or slightly better than, consensus expectations.
raw.outer_circle: Peripheral yields fell sharply (Spanish 10-year below 6%); European equities and bank stocks surged; the euro strengthened; the announcement marked a decisive de-escalation of eurozone tail risk.
raw.notes: Programme never activated but proved highly effective as a backstop.

raw.title: German Constitutional Court clears ESM with conditions
raw.description: Germany’s Federal Constitutional Court rejected injunctions against the European Stability Mechanism, allowing the permanent bailout fund to proceed while imposing parliamentary-control conditions.
raw.middle_circle: A negative ruling would have been a major setback; markets largely expected approval with conditions, reducing but not eliminating legal risk.
raw.outer_circle: Positive reaction in the euro and risk assets; the decision removed a key institutional obstacle ahead of the ECB’s OMT announcement.
raw.notes: Ruling issued 12 September; important legal clearance for the ESM.

raw.title: Federal Reserve launches open-ended QE3
raw.description: The FOMC announced it would purchase $40 billion per month of agency mortgage-backed securities on an open-ended basis and extended its forward guidance, stating that exceptionally low rates were likely warranted at least through mid-2015.
raw.middle_circle: Markets had priced a high probability of further easing; the open-ended structure and explicit link to labour-market improvement were more aggressive than many forecasts.
raw.outer_circle: Equities surged to multi-year highs; gold and other risk assets rose; the dollar weakened; Treasury yields initially rose as risk appetite improved.
raw.notes: Combined with ongoing Operation Twist, monthly longer-term purchases reached ~$85 billion through year-end.

raw.title: Spain announces further austerity and reform measures
raw.description: The Spanish government outlined additional fiscal and structural measures aimed at meeting deficit targets and satisfying conditions linked to European support, amid ongoing market scrutiny of its banking and sovereign finances.
raw.middle_circle: Further austerity was expected; credibility hinged on implementation capacity and growth impact.
raw.outer_circle: Limited immediate market relief; Spanish assets remained sensitive to broader eurozone developments and ECB backstop expectations.
raw.notes: Part of the ongoing Spanish adjustment programme.

raw.title: Hurricane Sandy forces two-day closure of U.S. equity markets
raw.description: Superstorm Sandy caused the first weather-related consecutive-day shutdown of U.S. stock exchanges since 1888, disrupting trading, settlement and corporate activity across the Northeast.
raw.middle_circle: Markets expected temporary disruption and sector-specific impacts (insurance losses, reconstruction demand); the multi-day closure itself was unprecedented in the modern era.
raw.outer_circle: Markets reopened with mixed-to-flat performance; home-improvement and generator stocks rose; insurers underperformed; broader indices stabilised quickly as the storm’s macro impact was judged limited.
raw.notes: Exchanges closed 29–30 October; reopened 31 October.

raw.title: U.S. markets reopen after Hurricane Sandy
raw.description: Equity markets resumed trading after the two-day weather closure, with sector rotation reflecting reconstruction demand and insurance exposure.
raw.middle_circle: Analysts expected limited lasting macro impact and short-term sector effects; historical hurricane studies suggested equities typically recover within months.
raw.outer_circle: Broad indices finished little changed; home-improvement and generator stocks outperformed; insurers lagged as loss estimates mounted.
raw.notes: First full session after the storm-related closure.

raw.title: Barack Obama re-elected President of the United States
raw.description: President Obama won a second term, defeating Republican challenger Mitt Romney. The result left divided government intact and focused markets on the approaching fiscal-cliff negotiations.
raw.middle_circle: Polling had pointed to a close race; markets had partially priced an Obama victory but remained focused on the fiscal-cliff deadline rather than the election itself.
raw.outer_circle: Equities initially sold off on concerns about higher taxes and regulation, then stabilised; sector rotation favoured healthcare and other Obama-policy beneficiaries.
raw.notes: Election night 6 November; market reaction unfolded on 7 November.

raw.title: Egyptian political crisis and constitutional decree spark market volatility
raw.description: President Morsi’s constitutional declaration expanding his powers triggered widespread protests and raised concerns about political stability and the IMF programme for Egypt, affecting regional risk sentiment.
raw.middle_circle: Markets had priced some post-Arab Spring political risk; the scale of the decree and subsequent unrest exceeded near-term expectations.
raw.outer_circle: Egyptian assets sold off; broader emerging-market risk appetite was modestly affected; the episode highlighted ongoing geopolitical fragility in the region.
sources: Contemporary news reports on Egyptian political crisis November 2012
raw.notes: Geopolitical event with limited but measurable EM impact.

raw.title: Federal Reserve expands QE3 and strengthens forward guidance
raw.description: The FOMC announced it would continue purchasing $40 billion of MBS and $45 billion of longer-term Treasuries per month after the conclusion of Operation Twist, and linked rate guidance more explicitly to unemployment and inflation thresholds.
raw.middle_circle: Further accommodation was widely expected; the shift to threshold-based guidance was viewed as an evolution of the mid-2015 calendar guidance.
raw.outer_circle: Risk assets remained well supported; the announcement reinforced the accommodative policy backdrop into year-end.
raw.notes: December FOMC meeting; built on the September QE3 decision.

raw.title: Central banks continue coordinated liquidity support measures
raw.description: Major central banks maintained and rolled over dollar-liquidity swap lines and other facilities to ensure adequate funding in global money markets amid residual eurozone stress.
raw.middle_circle: The facilities were already in place; markets viewed their continuation as a necessary backstop rather than a new stimulus.
raw.outer_circle: Money-market tensions remained contained; the measures supported overall financial stability into year-end.
raw.notes: Ongoing technical support rather than a discrete market-moving announcement.

raw.title: Liberal Democratic Party wins Japanese general election; Abe returns
raw.description: Shinzo Abe’s Liberal Democratic Party secured a landslide victory, paving the way for aggressive monetary easing, fiscal stimulus and structural reforms later known as Abenomics.
raw.middle_circle: Markets anticipated an LDP victory and a shift toward more aggressive policy; the margin of victory reinforced expectations of a major policy regime change.
raw.outer_circle: Yen weakened; Nikkei rallied strongly into year-end and early 2013 as markets priced in the forthcoming policy mix.
raw.notes: Election result set the stage for the 2013 policy shift.

raw.title: U.S. averts full fiscal cliff with last-minute tax deal
raw.description: Congress passed and the President signed legislation preventing the full set of tax increases and spending cuts scheduled for 1 January 2013, although sequestration spending cuts were only delayed.
raw.middle_circle: Markets expected a compromise; the final deal was narrower than some had hoped, leaving sequestration and the debt ceiling as unresolved risks for early 2013.
raw.outer_circle: Equities staged a late-year rally; the Dow posted its largest New Year’s Eve gain on record; risk assets finished 2012 with solid gains.
raw.notes: Agreement reached in the final hours of 2012; signed into law early 2013.

raw.title: U.S. averts fiscal cliff with last-minute tax deal
raw.description: Congress passed and the President signed legislation preventing the full set of automatic tax increases and spending cuts scheduled for 1 January 2013, although sequestration was only delayed. The deal raised taxes on high incomes and postponed some spending cuts.
raw.middle_circle: Markets expected a compromise but remained concerned about residual fiscal drag and the unresolved debt ceiling; many feared a deeper growth hit if no deal was reached.
raw.outer_circle: Global equities rallied sharply on the first trading day of 2013; oil and gold also rose; risk assets benefited from the removal of immediate uncertainty.
raw.notes: Agreement reached in the final hours of 2012; market reaction unfolded on 2 January 2013.

raw.title: ECB keeps rates unchanged amid improving eurozone sentiment
raw.description: The European Central Bank held its main refinancing rate steady while noting gradual stabilisation in the euro area, contributing to the broader reduction in peripheral risk premia that characterised early 2013.
raw.middle_circle: Markets expected continuity after Draghi’s 2012 commitments; any signal of further easing or tightening was closely watched.
raw.outer_circle: Limited immediate reaction; the broader trend of declining peripheral spreads continued.
raw.notes: Representative of the relatively calm early-2013 eurozone policy backdrop.

raw.title: Italian general election produces hung parliament
raw.description: Elections failed to produce a clear governing majority, with the centre-left, centre-right and anti-establishment Five Star Movement splitting the vote, raising concerns about political stability and reform momentum in the eurozone’s third-largest economy.
raw.middle_circle: Markets had hoped for a stable pro-reform government; the inconclusive result revived fears of policy paralysis.
raw.outer_circle: Italian yields rose; the euro and European equities weakened modestly; the reaction was contained relative to 2011–12 crisis peaks.
sources: Contemporary reports on Italian election February 2013
raw.notes: Political uncertainty persisted for weeks until a grand-coalition government was formed.

raw.title: Eurogroup announces Cyprus bailout including deposit levy
raw.description: Eurozone finance ministers agreed a €10 billion bailout for Cyprus that initially included a one-off levy on both insured and uninsured deposits, triggering deposit flight fears and a ten-day bank closure.
raw.middle_circle: Markets expected a conventional programme; the inclusion of a levy on insured deposits was a major surprise that raised systemic concerns about eurozone deposit safety.
raw.outer_circle: European bank shares fell sharply; the euro weakened; broader contagion remained limited after the levy on insured deposits was later dropped, but the episode introduced the concept of bail-in.
raw.notes: Initial package of 16 March; revised package sparing insured deposits agreed 25 March.

raw.title: Revised Cyprus bailout finalised with bail-in of uninsured deposits
raw.description: A modified programme was agreed under which Laiki Bank was resolved, uninsured depositors at Bank of Cyprus took large losses, and capital controls were imposed; insured deposits were protected.
raw.middle_circle: After the initial levy proposal was rejected, markets expected a solution focused on uninsured deposits and bank resolution; capital controls were a novel and worrying feature.
raw.outer_circle: Bank stocks stabilised relative to the prior week; the euro remained under pressure; the precedent of bail-in influenced later European bank resolution frameworks.
raw.notes: Banks reopened under capital controls on 28 March.

raw.title: Bank of Japan launches Quantitative and Qualitative Easing (QQE)
raw.description: Under new Governor Haruhiko Kuroda the BoJ announced a massive programme to double the monetary base, double JGB holdings, extend the average maturity of purchases, and buy ETFs and J-REITs, aiming for 2% inflation in about two years.
raw.middle_circle: Markets expected aggressive easing under Abenomics but the scale (especially the commitment to double the monetary base and lengthen maturities) exceeded most forecasts.
raw.outer_circle: Nikkei surged; the yen depreciated sharply; JGB yields initially fell then became highly volatile; the move triggered a global risk-on response and carry-trade flows.
raw.notes: First major policy action of the Kuroda era; widely described as exceeding expectations.

raw.title: Gold enters bear market and suffers multi-decade one-day crash
raw.description: Gold prices fell more than 20% from their 2011 peak, entering a bear market, and then plunged roughly 9% on 15 April in the largest one-day drop in three decades, driven by ETF outflows, lower bank forecasts and Cyprus-related gold-sale concerns.
raw.middle_circle: Many analysts had expected a gradual correction from elevated levels; the speed and magnitude of the April decline surprised both bulls and bears.
raw.outer_circle: Spot and futures gold collapsed; related equities and other commodities sold off; the episode marked the end of the multi-year gold bull market.
raw.notes: Key selling days 12 and 15 April; gold finished 2013 with its largest annual decline in more than three decades.

raw.title: Gold records largest one-day percentage decline in three decades
raw.description: Gold futures and spot prices plunged approximately 9% in a single session, the steepest daily drop since the early 1980s, amplifying the broader April sell-off and reinforcing the shift out of the metal.
raw.middle_circle: After the prior week’s decline, further technical selling and stop-loss cascades were possible but the magnitude still exceeded most forecasts.
raw.outer_circle: Panic selling and heavy volume; related commodities and risk assets also weakened; the day became emblematic of the 2013 gold bear market.
raw.notes: Continuation of the mid-April gold crash.

raw.title: FOMC statement first hints at possible adjustment of purchase pace
raw.description: The May FOMC statement introduced language that the Committee was prepared to increase or reduce the pace of purchases to maintain appropriate accommodation as the outlook evolved, marking an early signal of eventual tapering.
raw.middle_circle: The change was subtle; many participants did not immediately interpret it as the start of an exit discussion.
raw.outer_circle: Yields began a gradual rise that accelerated after Bernanke’s 22 May testimony; the statement is retrospectively viewed as the start of the taper-tantrum period.
raw.notes: Retrospective marker for the beginning of the 2013 taper tantrum window.

issues: Non-specific source description; documentary citation needed

raw.title: Bank of England maintains policy amid global yield pressures
raw.description: The Bank of England kept Bank Rate and asset-purchase targets unchanged while global fixed-income markets began to reprice in anticipation of eventual Fed tapering.
raw.middle_circle: UK policy was expected to remain accommodative; the dominant driver was U.S. monetary-policy expectations.
raw.outer_circle: Gilts sold off in sympathy with Treasuries; sterling was mixed; equity markets remained resilient.
sources: Bank of England monetary policy announcements 2013
raw.notes: Part of the broader global fixed-income adjustment in spring 2013.

raw.title: Bernanke signals possible taper of asset purchases
raw.description: In testimony before Congress, Federal Reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke stated that the FOMC could take a step down in the pace of purchases in the next few meetings if the labour market continued to improve, triggering the start of the ‘taper tantrum’.
raw.middle_circle: Markets had begun to discuss eventual tapering but most participants did not expect explicit near-term signalling; the comments were interpreted as more hawkish than anticipated.
raw.outer_circle: Treasury yields rose sharply; equities sold off; emerging-market currencies and bonds weakened; volatility increased across fixed-income and FX markets.
raw.notes: Widely regarded as the opening event of the 2013 taper tantrum.

raw.title: FOMC and Bernanke press conference intensify taper expectations
raw.description: The Federal Reserve kept policy unchanged but Bernanke’s post-meeting press conference outlined a possible path for reducing purchases later in 2013 and ending them around mid-2014 if the economy evolved as expected, reinforcing market concerns about tighter financial conditions.
raw.middle_circle: After the May testimony, markets expected clarification; the concrete timeline language was viewed as more definitive than many had priced.
raw.outer_circle: Yields spiked further; equities and emerging-market assets sold off; the episode produced one of the sharpest global fixed-income and FX adjustments of the year.
raw.notes: Key escalation of the taper tantrum.

raw.title: China interbank liquidity crisis – Shibor spikes to record highs
raw.description: Overnight and seven-day Shanghai Interbank Offered Rates surged to historic highs (overnight above 13%, repo rates briefly near 30%) as the People’s Bank of China initially refrained from injecting liquidity, exposing vulnerabilities in the shadow-banking and interbank funding system.
raw.middle_circle: Seasonal factors and regulatory tightening were known; the severity of the spike and the PBoC’s initial reluctance to ease surprised markets that had grown accustomed to accommodative liquidity management.
raw.outer_circle: Chinese equities sold off sharply; interbank activity contracted; global risk sentiment was affected; the PBoC later provided targeted support and the rates retreated.
raw.notes: Peak stress around 20 June; rates eased after PBoC communication and liquidity support later in the month.

raw.title: PBoC signals willingness to stabilise interbank liquidity
raw.description: After days of extreme stress, the People’s Bank of China communicated that overall liquidity was adequate and that it would use open-market operations and other tools to limit unusual volatility, helping rates retreat from record highs.
raw.middle_circle: Markets had begun to fear a prolonged credit crunch; the PBoC’s shift toward stabilisation language was interpreted as a de-escalation.
raw.outer_circle: Interbank rates declined from peaks; Chinese equities stabilised; global risk sentiment improved modestly.
raw.notes: Follow-on to the 20 June spike.

raw.title: Egyptian military removes President Morsi
raw.description: The Egyptian armed forces ousted elected President Mohamed Morsi following mass protests, suspending the constitution and installing an interim government, raising geopolitical and regional stability concerns.
raw.middle_circle: Political tension had been rising; markets priced elevated risk but the speed of the military intervention still produced a risk-off reaction in regional assets.
raw.outer_circle: Egyptian assets weakened; oil saw a modest geopolitical premium; broader emerging-market sentiment was already under pressure from the taper tantrum.
sources: Contemporary news reports on Egyptian coup July 2013
raw.notes: Geopolitical event with measurable but secondary market impact amid the larger taper narrative.

raw.title: Chemical weapons attack in Ghouta, Syria
raw.description: A large-scale sarin attack on the Damascus suburb of Ghouta killed hundreds of civilians, prompting the United States and allies to consider military strikes and elevating geopolitical risk premiums.
raw.middle_circle: Markets had monitored the Syrian civil war; the confirmed use of chemical weapons and the subsequent U.S. threat of force were viewed as a potential catalyst for broader regional escalation.
raw.outer_circle: Oil prices rose on supply-disruption fears; gold and safe-haven assets benefited; equities came under modest pressure until diplomatic solutions emerged.
raw.notes: Attack on 21 August; market focus intensified in late August and early September.

raw.title: Nasdaq trading halt due to technical glitch
raw.description: A technical problem halted trading in all Nasdaq-listed securities for approximately three hours, disrupting price discovery in major technology names and raising questions about market infrastructure resilience.
raw.middle_circle: Exchanges had experienced prior glitches; the duration and breadth of the halt exceeded recent incidents.
raw.outer_circle: Trading resumed later in the day; broader market impact was limited but the episode highlighted operational risk in electronic markets.
raw.notes: Primarily an operational rather than fundamental market event.

raw.title: G20 discussions and Syria diplomacy influence risk sentiment
raw.description: Meetings on the sidelines of the G20 summit contributed to the emerging U.S.–Russia understanding on Syrian chemical weapons, reducing the probability of imminent military action and supporting a broader improvement in risk appetite.
raw.middle_circle: Geopolitical risk had been elevated; any diplomatic progress was viewed positively by markets already positioning for a Fed no-taper outcome.
raw.outer_circle: Oil prices continued to ease; equities remained supported ahead of the mid-September FOMC meeting.
sources: Contemporary G20 and Syria diplomacy reporting September 2013
raw.notes: Part of the broader de-escalation of Syria risk.

raw.title: U.S.–Russia framework agreement on Syrian chemical weapons
raw.description: The United States and Russia agreed a framework for the accounting, inspection and elimination of Syria’s chemical weapons stockpile, averting an imminent U.S.-led military strike.
raw.middle_circle: Markets had priced a high probability of limited strikes; the diplomatic off-ramp was a positive surprise that removed a near-term geopolitical risk premium.
raw.outer_circle: Oil prices fell sharply; risk assets recovered; gold gave back safe-haven gains.
raw.notes: Framework announced mid-September; formal UN resolution followed later in the month.

raw.title: Federal Reserve surprises markets by not tapering
raw.description: The FOMC decided to maintain the $85 billion monthly pace of asset purchases, citing the need for more evidence of sustained improvement in the labour market and the potential impact of fiscal tightening, contrary to widespread expectations of a reduction.
raw.middle_circle: After months of taper signalling, a clear majority of market participants expected the Fed to reduce purchases by $10–15 billion; the decision not to taper was a major positive surprise.
raw.outer_circle: Equities rallied to new highs; Treasury yields fell; the dollar weakened; emerging-market assets and gold rebounded sharply.
raw.notes: One of the largest policy surprises of 2013; reversed much of the summer taper-tantrum price action.

raw.title: U.S. federal government enters partial shutdown
raw.description: Failure to pass appropriations legislation led to the first partial government shutdown since 1996, furloughing hundreds of thousands of federal employees and suspending non-essential services.
raw.middle_circle: Markets expected a short-lived shutdown; historical precedents suggested limited lasting equity-market impact if resolved quickly.
raw.outer_circle: Equities initially shrugged off the event; the dollar weakened; concern later intensified as the debt-ceiling deadline approached.
raw.notes: Shutdown began 1 October and lasted until 17 October.

raw.title: Congress reaches deal to end shutdown and raise debt ceiling
raw.description: Lawmakers agreed to fund the government through mid-January 2014 and suspend the debt ceiling through early February, ending the 16-day shutdown and averting a potential U.S. default.
raw.middle_circle: Markets had grown increasingly concerned as the 17 October debt-ceiling deadline approached; a last-minute deal was widely expected but the timing remained uncertain.
raw.outer_circle: Equities rallied strongly; volatility fell; Treasury bills and short-term funding markets normalised; risk assets recovered the earlier pull-back.
raw.notes: Deal announced 16 October; signed into law shortly thereafter.

raw.title: Debt-ceiling suspension and government reopening take effect
raw.description: Following the 16 October agreement, the government reopened and the debt ceiling was suspended, removing the immediate threat of default and allowing normal federal operations to resume.
raw.middle_circle: Markets had largely priced the deal after the prior day’s announcement; residual uncertainty centred on the short-term nature of the extension.
raw.outer_circle: Risk assets continued to recover; short-term Treasury bill dislocations normalised; focus shifted back to monetary policy and growth data.
raw.notes: Operational implementation of the 16 October political agreement.

raw.title: Super Typhoon Haiyan makes landfall
raw.description: One of the strongest tropical cyclones on record struck the central Philippines, causing catastrophic damage, thousands of deaths and significant economic losses, with secondary effects on regional supply chains and insurance markets.
raw.middle_circle: Markets expected a severe humanitarian and local economic impact; global financial-market spillovers were anticipated to be limited.
raw.outer_circle: Local equities and insurers reacted; broader global risk assets showed only modest sensitivity.
raw.notes: Primarily a humanitarian and regional economic event with limited global market footprint.

raw.title: U.S. regulators finalise Volcker Rule
raw.description: Five federal agencies approved the final Volcker Rule, restricting proprietary trading by banks and limiting certain relationships with hedge funds and private-equity funds, completing a major piece of post-crisis regulatory reform.
raw.middle_circle: The rule had been long anticipated; final details on market-making exemptions and compliance timelines were closely watched by bank equity and credit investors.
raw.outer_circle: Bank stocks showed limited immediate reaction; the longer-term impact was expected to reduce trading revenues and increase compliance costs.
raw.notes: Implementation phased in over subsequent years.

raw.title: Federal Reserve begins tapering asset purchases
raw.description: The FOMC announced it would reduce monthly asset purchases by $10 billion to $75 billion beginning in January 2014, while strengthening forward guidance on the federal funds rate and emphasising that the reduction did not signal an imminent rate hike.
raw.middle_circle: After the September surprise, markets had re-priced the likelihood of a December start; the decision was largely anticipated and accompanied by dovish guidance.
raw.outer_circle: Equities rallied to new highs; yields were little changed or edged lower; the orderly reaction contrasted sharply with the summer taper tantrum.
raw.notes: Bernanke’s final major policy decision; markets digested the news calmly.

raw.title: U.S. equities close out strongest year since 1990s
raw.description: The S&P 500 finished 2013 with a gain of approximately 30%, the Dow roughly 26%, and the Nasdaq more than 38%, marking one of the strongest calendar-year performances of the post-crisis bull market despite multiple political and policy shocks.
raw.middle_circle: By year-end most strategists expected solid but not spectacular gains; the actual magnitude exceeded many beginning-of-year forecasts.
raw.outer_circle: Year-end positioning and the orderly start of tapering supported continued risk appetite; volatility remained relatively subdued.
raw.notes: Year-end close reflecting the cumulative resilience of equity markets in 2013.

raw.title: Janet Yellen becomes Chair of the Federal Reserve
raw.description: Janet Yellen succeeded Ben Bernanke as Chair of the Board of Governors, becoming the first woman to lead the Federal Reserve and inheriting the task of managing the ongoing taper and eventual normalisation of policy.
raw.middle_circle: Yellen was widely expected to continue the existing policy trajectory; markets focused on her communication style and any nuance on the labour-market reaction function.
raw.outer_circle: Limited immediate price reaction; her early testimony and press conferences were closely watched for signals on the pace of tapering and rate-hike timing.
sources: Federal Reserve historical records; contemporary reporting January 2014
raw.notes: Formal transition effective 1 February 2014 after Senate confirmation.

raw.title: Unmarked forces seize Crimean infrastructure
raw.description: Armed personnel without insignia took control of key government buildings and airports in Crimea, marking the start of Russia’s military intervention in the Ukrainian peninsula and triggering the most serious European security crisis in decades.
raw.middle_circle: Markets had monitored Ukrainian political turmoil but underestimated the speed and scale of direct Russian military involvement in Crimea.
raw.outer_circle: Russian stocks and the ruble sold off sharply; European equities, particularly those with Russian exposure, declined; safe-haven flows supported Treasuries and the dollar.
raw.notes: Initial seizures on 27–28 February; full annexation process followed in March.

raw.title: Russian markets plunge on Ukraine military escalation fears
raw.description: Russian equities suffered one of their worst single-day declines in years and the ruble hit multi-year lows as investors priced the risk of broader conflict and Western sanctions following the Crimea intervention.
raw.middle_circle: Analysts expected volatility but the magnitude of the equity and currency moves reflected heightened fear of military escalation and capital flight.
raw.outer_circle: RTS index fell more than 10% at one point; the central bank hiked rates; European indices with energy exposure also declined before partial recovery.
raw.notes: Peak fear day in early March; markets later stabilised as immediate wider invasion fears eased.

raw.title: Russia annexes Crimea; first round of Western sanctions
raw.description: Following the Crimean referendum, Russia formally annexed the peninsula. The United States and European Union imposed initial asset freezes and travel bans. The ruble and Russian equities began a sustained decline that accelerated later in the year with oil-price collapse.
raw.middle_circle: Many investors still priced a limited diplomatic confrontation; full annexation and meaningful financial sanctions were assigned low probability.
raw.outer_circle: Ruble and equity markets sold off immediately, capital outflows accelerated, and the subsequent sanctions-plus-oil combination produced a far deeper currency and growth shock than pre-annexation positioning implied.
raw.notes: Russia geopolitical trigger. FX and equity reaction used as proxies.

raw.title: Russia formally annexes Crimea
raw.description: Following a referendum that Western governments deemed illegitimate, President Putin signed a treaty incorporating Crimea into the Russian Federation, prompting the first round of targeted Western sanctions.
raw.middle_circle: Markets had largely priced the annexation itself; the key uncertainty was the severity and scope of forthcoming sanctions.
raw.outer_circle: Initial risk-off reaction was limited; Russian assets stabilised relative to early-March extremes as sanctions proved narrower than worst-case fears.
raw.notes: Formal annexation completed mid-March; sanctions escalated later in the year.

raw.title: Energy Future Holdings files for bankruptcy
raw.description: Texas power company Energy Future Holdings, burdened by more than $40 billion in debt taken on in a leveraged buyout, filed one of the largest corporate bankruptcies in U.S. history amid low natural-gas prices and structural challenges.
raw.middle_circle: A restructuring had been widely expected; the formal filing removed uncertainty about the timing of the process.
raw.outer_circle: Limited broad-market impact; high-yield energy credit continued to reflect stress from low commodity prices later in the year.
raw.notes: One of the largest bankruptcies of the post-crisis period.

raw.title: Thai military stages coup
raw.description: The Thai army declared martial law and seized power, ending months of political unrest and installing a military government, prompting short-term risk aversion toward Southeast Asian assets.
raw.middle_circle: Political instability had been ongoing; a formal coup was a downside scenario that markets partially anticipated.
raw.outer_circle: Thai assets sold off initially then stabilised; broader emerging-market impact was limited.
sources: Contemporary reporting on Thai coup May 2014
raw.notes: Geopolitical event with primarily local market consequences.

raw.location_name: Kinshasa / Copperbelt, Democratic Republic of the Congo
raw.title: Commodity-price collapse hits DRC copper and cobalt revenues
raw.description: The mid-2010s commodity supercycle peak gave way to a sharp decline in copper and cobalt prices. The Congolese franc depreciated further and fiscal revenues from the mining sector contracted, amplifying domestic monetary pressures.
raw.middle_circle: Consensus expected a moderate correction in industrial metals with limited lasting impact on DRC fiscal and FX stability.
raw.outer_circle: The franc’s depreciation and mining-revenue shortfall were deeper and more persistent than the soft-landing paths priced at the supercycle peak.
raw.notes: Central African commodity-FX linkage. Price and FX reaction used as proxies.

raw.title: Oil-price collapse begins Venezuela’s economic free-fall
raw.description: Global oil prices began a multi-year slide from above $100. Venezuela, already suffering production declines and fiscal imbalances, entered a period of accelerating inflation, shortages and GDP contraction that ultimately led to hyperinflation.
raw.middle_circle: Consensus expected oil to stabilise at still-elevated levels sufficient to fund Venezuela’s spending; a sustained sub-$50 environment and production collapse were outside the base case.
raw.outer_circle: Fiscal revenues collapsed, money-printing accelerated, and the parallel exchange rate began a multi-year depreciation far steeper than any official or market forecast had contemplated.
raw.notes: Critical commodity trigger for Venezuela’s collapse. Parallel-rate and inflation path used as proxies.

raw.title: ECB cuts rates and introduces negative deposit facility rate
raw.description: The European Central Bank lowered its main refinancing rate to 0.15% and cut the deposit facility rate to –0.10%, becoming the first major central bank to impose a negative rate on bank reserves, while also announcing further credit-easing measures.
raw.middle_circle: A rate cut into negative territory was widely expected; markets focused on whether Draghi would also signal readiness for large-scale asset purchases.
raw.outer_circle: The euro fell to multi-month lows; European equities rose; peripheral spreads tightened modestly as the package was seen as a step toward further easing.
raw.notes: Historic first negative deposit rate for a major central bank.

raw.title: Brent crude peaks near $115 before multi-month collapse begins
raw.description: Brent front-month futures reached their 2014 high above $115 per barrel amid geopolitical risk premiums, after which a combination of rising U.S. shale supply, resilient OPEC output and softening demand expectations triggered a sustained price decline.
raw.middle_circle: Many analysts expected oil to remain range-bound near $100–110; few anticipated the scale of the subsequent supply-driven collapse.
raw.outer_circle: Prices began a multi-month descent that would eventually more than halve the value of crude; energy equities and related currencies came under progressive pressure.
raw.notes: Peak around 19–20 June; the decline accelerated in the second half of the year.

raw.title: Malaysia Airlines Flight MH17 shot down over eastern Ukraine
raw.description: A civilian airliner was destroyed by a surface-to-air missile over rebel-held territory in eastern Ukraine, killing all 298 people on board and sharply escalating international tension with Russia.
raw.middle_circle: Markets had already priced ongoing conflict risk; the downing of a civilian aircraft raised the probability of broader sanctions and diplomatic isolation of Russia.
raw.outer_circle: Russian assets sold off; European risk sentiment weakened; airline stocks were pressured; the event contributed to further Western sanctions later in the summer.
sources: Contemporary news reports on MH17 and market reaction July 2014
raw.notes: Geopolitical catalyst that intensified the sanctions regime against Russia.

raw.title: Argentina defaults on sovereign debt for second time in 13 years
raw.description: Argentina entered technical default after failing to reach agreement with holdout creditors, triggering cross-default clauses and renewing focus on emerging-market sovereign risk.
raw.middle_circle: A default had been widely anticipated after court rulings favoured holdouts; the main uncertainty was the duration and eventual resolution terms.
raw.outer_circle: Argentine assets sold off; broader emerging-market contagion remained limited; the event reinforced caution toward high-yield sovereign credit.
raw.notes: Second default since 2001; resolved years later via settlement.
