raw.title: United States and EU impose broader sectoral sanctions on Russia
raw.description: Western governments expanded sanctions to target Russian energy, defence and financial sectors in response to the ongoing conflict in eastern Ukraine and the downing of MH17, increasing pressure on the Russian economy.
raw.middle_circle: Further sanctions had been anticipated; the inclusion of major energy and banking entities raised the expected economic cost for Russia.
raw.outer_circle: Russian assets weakened further; European companies with significant Russian exposure underperformed; the measures compounded the later impact of falling oil prices.
raw.notes: Part of the escalating sanctions regime throughout 2014.

raw.title: Bank of America reaches record $16.65 billion mortgage settlement
raw.description: Bank of America agreed to pay $16.65 billion to resolve federal and state claims related to the sale of toxic mortgage securities, the largest civil settlement with a single entity in U.S. history at the time.
raw.middle_circle: A large settlement had been expected; the final size was at the upper end of estimates and removed a major legal overhang.
raw.outer_circle: BAC shares reacted relatively constructively as uncertainty was resolved; the settlement was viewed as a step toward clearing crisis-era liabilities.
raw.notes: Part of the broader wave of large bank settlements in 2014.

issues: Non-specific source description; documentary citation needed

raw.title: ECB cuts rates further and announces ABS and covered-bond purchase programmes
raw.description: The ECB lowered the deposit rate to –0.20% and the main refinancing rate to 0.05%, while unveiling plans to purchase asset-backed securities and covered bonds as additional easing measures short of full sovereign QE.
raw.middle_circle: Further easing was expected; markets scrutinised whether the measures would be large enough to address low inflation without sovereign-bond purchases.
raw.outer_circle: The euro weakened; European risk assets benefited modestly; the steps were viewed as incremental progress toward more aggressive stimulus.
raw.notes: Follow-on to the June negative-rate decision.

raw.title: Scottish independence referendum: No vote prevails
raw.description: Scottish voters rejected independence by approximately 55% to 45%, removing the immediate risk of the break-up of the United Kingdom and associated currency and institutional uncertainty.
raw.middle_circle: Late polls had shown a possible Yes victory, elevating sterling volatility and pressure on Scottish-exposed stocks; a clear No outcome was the market’s preferred scenario.
raw.outer_circle: Sterling spiked higher; Scottish bank and insurer shares rallied; UK equities rose modestly as political risk premium compressed.
raw.notes: Result confirmed in the early hours of 19 September.

raw.title: Alibaba completes record $25 billion IPO
raw.description: Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba Group priced its IPO at $68 per share and began trading on the NYSE, raising approximately $25 billion (including greenshoe) and closing the first day up 38%, valuing the company at over $230 billion.
raw.middle_circle: Demand was expected to be strong; the final size and first-day pop exceeded many forecasts, making it the largest IPO in history at the time.
raw.outer_circle: Shares opened well above the offer price and closed near $94; related Chinese internet names and the broader IPO market received a positive sentiment boost.
raw.notes: Largest IPO on record at the time; underwriters exercised the greenshoe option.

issues: Non-specific source description; documentary citation needed

raw.title: Umbrella Movement protests erupt in Hong Kong
raw.description: Large-scale pro-democracy demonstrations began in Hong Kong after Beijing’s restrictive framework for the 2017 chief-executive election, raising concerns about political stability and the city’s role as a financial hub.
raw.middle_circle: Political tensions had been building; the scale and duration of street occupations exceeded near-term expectations.
raw.outer_circle: Hong Kong equities experienced bouts of volatility; the broader China and EM impact remained contained as protests stayed largely peaceful.
sources: Contemporary reporting on Hong Kong Umbrella Movement 2014
raw.notes: Protests continued for several weeks into October–November.

raw.title: First diagnosed Ebola case in the United States heightens market fears
raw.description: Confirmation of the first Ebola case diagnosed on U.S. soil (in Texas) amplified investor concerns about the potential spread of the West African outbreak, contributing to risk-off flows alongside other macro worries.
raw.middle_circle: Markets had monitored the African outbreak; a domestic U.S. case raised the perceived probability of broader disruption to travel and economic activity.
raw.outer_circle: Airline and travel stocks sold off; certain biotech and protective-equipment names surged; broader equity indices came under pressure in early October.
raw.notes: Part of a broader October risk-off episode that also involved Europe and U.S. data concerns.

raw.title: Global equities suffer sharp intra-day sell-off on growth and Ebola fears
raw.description: A confluence of weak U.S. data, European growth concerns, and lingering Ebola anxiety triggered one of the most volatile sessions of the year, with the Dow briefly down more than 460 points before recovering a large portion of losses.
raw.middle_circle: Markets were already on edge after a multi-week correction; the combination of data and geopolitical/health headlines produced an outsized fear response.
raw.outer_circle: Major indices plunged then staged a late rebound; volatility spiked; the episode marked the low point of the autumn correction before a strong year-end rally.
raw.notes: Key day in the mid-October 2014 market turbulence.

raw.title: Ebola case confirmed in New York City
raw.description: A doctor who had treated Ebola patients in West Africa tested positive for the virus in New York, renewing public and market concern about the domestic spread of the outbreak.
raw.middle_circle: After earlier U.S. cases, another diagnosis in a major city was expected to produce sector-specific volatility rather than broad market disruption.
raw.outer_circle: Travel-related stocks came under pressure; selected healthcare and equipment names rose; broader indices showed limited lasting impact.
raw.notes: Part of the series of U.S. Ebola-related market reactions in autumn 2014.

raw.title: Federal Reserve ends QE3 asset purchases
raw.description: The FOMC announced the conclusion of its third round of quantitative easing, citing substantial improvement in the labour market, while maintaining that the federal funds rate would remain near zero for a “considerable time.”
raw.middle_circle: The end of purchases was fully anticipated; attention focused on the tone of the statement regarding the economic outlook and rate-guidance language.
raw.outer_circle: Markets reacted calmly; the dollar strengthened modestly; equities were mixed to slightly lower as focus shifted toward the timing of eventual rate hikes.
raw.notes: Marked the formal end of the Fed’s post-crisis large-scale asset purchase programmes.

raw.title: Bank of Japan unexpectedly expands Quantitative and Qualitative Easing
raw.description: In a surprise 5–4 decision the BoJ accelerated the pace of monetary-base expansion to about ¥80 trillion annually, increased JGB purchases, extended maturities, and raised ETF and J-REIT buying targets, catching markets off guard.
raw.middle_circle: Most analysts expected no change; the expansion was a clear positive surprise timed just after the Fed ended QE.
raw.outer_circle: Nikkei surged nearly 5% to multi-year highs; the yen weakened sharply; global risk assets rallied in a coordinated move.
raw.notes: Often called the “Halloween surprise”; coincided with GPIF portfolio shift announcement.

raw.title: Japan’s GPIF announces major shift toward equities
raw.description: The Government Pension Investment Fund, the world’s largest pension fund, detailed plans to roughly double its target allocation to domestic and international equities, amplifying the impact of the BoJ’s simultaneous easing expansion.
raw.middle_circle: A portfolio reallocation had been anticipated under Abenomics; the scale and timing alongside the BoJ move exceeded expectations.
raw.outer_circle: Japanese and global equities extended gains; the combined BoJ–GPIF announcements produced one of the strongest risk-on days of the year.
raw.notes: Announcement closely followed the BoJ decision on 31 October.

raw.title: OPEC decision not to cut output accelerates oil-price collapse
raw.description: OPEC, led by Saudi Arabia, opted to defend market share rather than cut production. Oil prices entered a multi-year slide that severely strained fiscal balances across Gulf and other Middle Eastern producers.
raw.middle_circle: Many market participants still expected a coordinated cut once prices approached $70–80; an explicit market-share strategy was a material surprise.
raw.outer_circle: Oil prices fell further and faster than consensus models projected, forcing large fiscal adjustments and equity underperformance across the region.
raw.notes: Saudi/OPEC policy event with region-wide fiscal and market consequences. Oil-price path used as proxy.

raw.title: OPEC decides against production cut despite falling prices
raw.description: OPEC ministers, led by Saudi Arabia, chose to maintain existing production levels rather than cut output in response to the oil-price decline, confirming a market-share strategy that accelerated the price collapse.
raw.middle_circle: Many participants had hoped for at least a modest cut; the decision to hold output was interpreted as the start of a price war with U.S. shale.
raw.outer_circle: Oil prices fell sharply in subsequent sessions; energy equities and the currencies of oil exporters (including the ruble) came under intense pressure.
raw.notes: Critical catalyst that transformed a gradual decline into a full-scale oil-price rout.

raw.title: Oil-price collapse triggers Canadian energy-sector and CAD stress
raw.description: OPEC’s decision not to cut production accelerated the slide in crude prices that had begun mid-year. Canadian energy equities, the TSX, and the Canadian dollar came under sustained pressure, ultimately contributing to a 2015 technical recession concentrated in Alberta.
raw.middle_circle: Many analysts expected a moderate correction in oil with limited spill-over to the broader Canadian economy given non-energy diversification.
raw.outer_circle: Energy stocks and CAD sold off more sharply and for longer than consensus models projected; capital expenditure collapsed and regional unemployment rose faster than the soft-landing scenarios that had dominated forecasts.
raw.notes: Canada-specific commodity channel. Price reaction in energy equities and CAD used as proxy.

issues: Non-specific source description; documentary citation needed

raw.title: ECB signals readiness to expand asset purchases if needed
raw.description: In its December meeting the ECB reiterated its willingness to use additional unconventional tools, including potentially larger-scale asset purchases, if the inflation outlook failed to improve, keeping markets focused on possible sovereign QE in 2015.
raw.middle_circle: Further easing language was expected; the explicit openness to expanding purchases supported the view that full QE remained a live option.
raw.outer_circle: The euro remained under pressure; peripheral spreads stayed contained; risk assets were supported by the accommodative signal.
raw.notes: Set the stage for the January 2015 sovereign QE announcement.

raw.title: Russian ruble crisis peak – overnight rate hike to 17%
raw.description: With oil below $60 and sanctions biting, the ruble entered freefall. The Central Bank of Russia raised its key rate from 10.5% to 17% in an emergency overnight move. The currency still lost ~20% in a single day at the worst point, triggering consumer panic and bank runs.
raw.middle_circle: Markets expected further gradual tightening and continued reserve defence; an emergency 650 bp hike and near-collapse of the currency were outside consensus scenarios.
raw.outer_circle: Ruble gapped lower despite the hike, equity and bond markets seized, and the scale of reserve burn and inflation surge exceeded every pre-crisis stress test.
raw.notes: Peak of the 2014–15 Russian currency crisis. Intraday FX move and rate response used as proxies.

issues: Non-specific source description; documentary citation needed

raw.title: Russian ruble crisis – “Black Tuesday”
raw.description: The ruble suffered its largest one-day decline in years, at one point losing more than 20% against the dollar intraday, as the combination of falling oil prices, sanctions and capital outflows overwhelmed market interventions.
raw.middle_circle: Further ruble weakness was expected, but the speed and scale of the December move exceeded most forecasts and raised concerns about financial stability.
raw.outer_circle: The central bank hiked rates aggressively; equity markets swung wildly; the episode highlighted the dual shock of sanctions and the oil-price collapse for Russia.
sources: Contemporary reports on Russian currency crisis December 2014
raw.notes: Peak stress around 15–16 December; rates were raised to 17%.

raw.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average closes above 18,000 for first time
raw.description: The Dow surpassed the 18,000 level for the first time, reflecting the resilience of U.S. equities despite the oil-price collapse, geopolitical tensions and the end of Fed asset purchases.
raw.middle_circle: A new high was consistent with the year’s strong performance; the milestone was largely symbolic amid ongoing debates about valuation and global growth risks.
raw.outer_circle: Equities continued to grind higher into year-end; the advance underscored the divergence between U.S. and many international markets.
raw.notes: Psychological milestone in a year of record equity highs.

raw.title: U.S. equities close 2014 with solid gains despite oil crash and geopolitics
raw.description: The S&P 500 finished the year up approximately 11–13% (price and total return), the Dow up roughly 7–8%, and the Nasdaq more than 13%, extending the post-crisis bull market through multiple geopolitical and commodity shocks.
raw.middle_circle: Most strategists had expected positive but more moderate returns; the resilience in the face of the oil-price collapse and Russia/Ukraine tensions exceeded many forecasts.
raw.outer_circle: Year-end positioning remained constructive; U.S. equities diverged positively from many commodity-linked and emerging markets.
raw.notes: Year-end close reflecting the overall strength of U.S. risk assets in 2014.

raw.title: Charlie Hebdo terrorist attack
raw.description: Gunmen attacked the offices of the satirical magazine Charlie Hebdo in Paris, killing 12 people. The attack raised short-term European security and political-risk concerns.
raw.middle_circle: No prior market pricing of a high-profile attack in central Paris.
raw.outer_circle: French equities and the euro experienced a brief risk-off move that was quickly reversed.
raw.notes: Attack occurred mid-morning local time.

raw.title: SNB abandons EUR/CHF exchange-rate floor
raw.description: The Swiss National Bank unexpectedly discontinued its minimum exchange rate of 1.20 francs per euro, a policy in place since September 2011, and simultaneously cut the interest rate on sight deposits to -0.75 percent. The move was made outside a scheduled meeting and came days after officials had described the floor as a cornerstone of policy.
raw.middle_circle: Markets widely expected the SNB to maintain the floor at least until after the ECB’s anticipated QE announcement the following week; the floor had been repeatedly defended as essential.
raw.outer_circle: EUR/CHF collapsed from 1.20 to as low as 0.85 within minutes, a roughly 30 percent move; Swiss equities plunged more than 8 percent and several FX brokers suffered large losses from stop-outs and liquidity gaps.
raw.notes: Exact announcement time confirmed as 09:30 UK time.

raw.title: ECB announces expanded asset-purchase programme (QE)
raw.description: The European Central Bank unveiled a sovereign-bond purchase programme of €60 billion per month starting in March 2015 and running at least until September 2016. Combined with existing private-sector purchases the total monthly injection was larger than many forecasts.
raw.middle_circle: Analysts expected a programme of around €50 billion per month; some doubted the ECB would buy sovereign bonds given German opposition.
raw.outer_circle: The euro fell more than two cents against the dollar, peripheral bond yields dropped to record lows and European equities rallied to multi-year highs on the larger-than-expected size.
raw.notes: Press conference began at 14:30 CET.

raw.title: Syriza wins Greek parliamentary election
raw.description: The left-wing Syriza party, led by Alexis Tsipras, won a snap election on an anti-austerity platform, ending the previous coalition government. The result immediately raised the prospect of confrontation with euro-area creditors and possible Grexit.
raw.middle_circle: Polls had pointed to a Syriza victory but markets had priced in a more moderate outcome or a coalition that would continue existing programmes.
raw.outer_circle: Greek stocks and bonds sold off sharply; euro-area peripheral spreads widened and the euro weakened on renewed sovereign-risk fears.
raw.notes: Official results confirmed late evening local time.

raw.title: ECB begins sovereign-bond purchases under QE
raw.description: The Eurosystem started buying euro-area government bonds as part of the expanded asset-purchase programme announced in January. Monthly purchases of €60 billion commenced.
raw.middle_circle: The start date had been signalled; the market impact was expected to be already largely priced.
raw.outer_circle: Peripheral spreads continued to compress and the euro remained under pressure as the actual flow of purchases began.
raw.notes: Purchases began in the week of 9 March.

raw.title: Royal Dutch Shell agrees to acquire BG Group
raw.description: Shell announced an all-share-and-cash takeover of BG Group valued at approximately £47 billion, one of the largest energy deals on record. The combination was intended to strengthen Shell’s LNG and deep-water positions amid falling oil prices.
raw.middle_circle: A deal had been rumoured but the size and timing surprised many given the oil-price collapse.
raw.outer_circle: BG shares jumped more than 30 percent; Shell shares initially fell on concerns about the premium paid at a time of low oil prices.
raw.notes: Announcement made before London open.

raw.title: German 10-year Bund yield hits record low
raw.description: The 10-year German government bond yield fell to 0.05 percent, the lowest in history, as ECB QE and deflation fears drove a relentless rally. The move later reversed violently in the so-called Bund tantrum.
raw.middle_circle: Many investors expected yields to go negative given the ECB’s purchase programme.
raw.outer_circle: The subsequent sell-off in May–June saw the 10-year yield rebound almost 100 basis points in a matter of weeks, one of the sharpest bond-market reversals of the year.
raw.notes: Exact intra-day low occurred during European hours.

raw.title: Conservative Party wins UK general election outright
raw.description: David Cameron’s Conservative Party secured an unexpected majority, ending five years of coalition government. The result removed immediate political uncertainty but raised the prospect of an EU-membership referendum.
raw.middle_circle: Most polls and betting markets had pointed to another hung parliament or a Labour-led coalition.
raw.outer_circle: Sterling and UK equities rallied sharply in overnight trading as the majority outcome reduced near-term political risk.
raw.notes: Exit poll and results emerged after 22:00 BST.

raw.title: Shanghai Composite reaches 2015 peak
raw.description: The Shanghai Composite Index hit an intra-day high of 5,178, completing a more than 150 percent rally from mid-2014. The surge had been fuelled by margin lending, retail participation and official encouragement.
raw.middle_circle: Many domestic commentators and some official media still described valuations as reasonable; international investors were more sceptical.
raw.outer_circle: The peak marked the start of a violent unwind; the index would lose more than 40 percent over the following three months.
raw.notes: Peak occurred during the Shanghai morning session.

raw.title: China stocks suffer worst week since financial crisis
raw.description: The Shanghai Composite fell 6.4 percent on the day and 13.3 percent for the week, its steepest weekly decline since 2008. Forced liquidation of margin positions accelerated the drop after the regulator tightened leverage rules.
raw.middle_circle: After the June 12 peak, many expected only a modest correction given continued policy support.
raw.outer_circle: Panic selling hit daily limit-down on hundreds of stocks; the move marked the beginning of a broader emerging-market and commodity sell-off.

raw.title: Shanghai Composite plunges 7.4 percent
raw.description: Chinese stocks recorded their largest one-day drop since 2008 as margin calls intensified. Roughly 2,000 stocks hit their 10 percent daily limit. The two-week decline from the June 12 high reached 19 percent.
raw.middle_circle: Weekend rate-cut hopes had been expected to stabilise the market.
raw.outer_circle: The sell-off spilled into commodity prices and other Asian equities; global risk appetite deteriorated.

raw.title: PBOC cuts rates and reserve requirements
raw.description: After a 19 percent two-week plunge in stocks, the People’s Bank of China cut benchmark lending and deposit rates and reduced the reserve-requirement ratio for selected banks in an attempt to stabilise markets.
raw.middle_circle: Further easing had been anticipated but the combination of rate and RRR cuts was larger than some forecasts.
raw.outer_circle: The Shanghai Composite briefly rallied then reversed, illustrating the limited effectiveness of traditional tools against a leverage unwind.
raw.notes: Announcement made over the weekend before Monday open.

raw.title: Greece misses IMF payment and enters arrears
raw.description: Greece failed to repay a €1.5 billion instalment to the IMF, becoming the first advanced economy to fall into arrears with the Fund. The country’s second bailout programme also expired the same day, leaving Athens without official financing.
raw.middle_circle: A last-minute extension or payment had been widely hoped for after weeks of talks.
raw.outer_circle: Greek two-year yields spiked above 40 percent; euro-area bank shares and peripheral bonds sold off, though contagion remained contained relative to 2012.
raw.notes: IMF confirmation came shortly after 22:00 GMT.

raw.title: Greek referendum rejects creditor terms
raw.description: Greek voters overwhelmingly rejected the latest austerity package proposed by euro-area creditors. Prime Minister Tsipras had framed the vote as a mandate to renegotiate, but the result increased the risk of Grexit.
raw.middle_circle: Opinion polls had been mixed; many investors expected a narrow “Yes” or a result that would force a compromise.
raw.outer_circle: European equities and the euro initially sold off but the reaction was milder than feared; Greek bank stocks remained suspended.
raw.notes: Results emerged Sunday evening.

raw.title: Eurozone leaders agree third Greek bailout
raw.description: After an all-night summit, euro-area leaders reached a provisional agreement on a third programme of up to €86 billion. Greece accepted most of the creditors’ demands, including further austerity and privatisation, in exchange for remaining in the euro.
raw.middle_circle: Many analysts had assigned a high probability to Grexit after the referendum.
raw.outer_circle: European risk assets rallied and Greek bond yields collapsed from crisis levels; the euro recovered some of its earlier losses.
raw.notes: Agreement reached in the early hours of 13 July.

raw.title: Iran nuclear deal (JCPOA) reached
raw.description: Iran and the P5+1 powers finalised a comprehensive agreement limiting Iran’s nuclear programme in exchange for sanctions relief. Implementation would allow Iran to increase oil exports once sanctions were lifted.
raw.middle_circle: A deal had been expected but the timing and the speed of potential Iranian oil-supply recovery were uncertain.
raw.outer_circle: Oil prices came under additional pressure on the prospect of extra Iranian barrels returning to an already oversupplied market.
raw.notes: Announcement made overnight in Vienna.

raw.title: PBOC devalues yuan and changes fixing mechanism
raw.description: The People’s Bank of China lowered the daily yuan midpoint by a record 1.9 percent and announced that the fixing would henceforth be more market-determined. The move was the largest one-day adjustment since 1994.
raw.middle_circle: Most observers expected only gradual, small adjustments; a sudden 2 percent devaluation was not priced in.
raw.outer_circle: The onshore and offshore yuan fell sharply, commodity currencies and emerging-market assets sold off, and global equities began a multi-week decline.
raw.notes: Fixing announced at the usual morning time in Beijing.

raw.title: China Black Monday and global equity crash
raw.description: The Shanghai Composite dropped 8.5 percent, its largest one-day fall since 2007. The move triggered a worldwide equity sell-off; the Dow Jones opened down more than 1,000 points, the first such drop in four years.
raw.middle_circle: After earlier interventions, many expected Chinese authorities to prevent another large decline.
raw.outer_circle: Circuit breakers and liquidity gaps appeared in US futures; the S&P 500 entered a 12 percent correction from its recent high and volatility spiked.
raw.notes: Shanghai session decline led the global move.

raw.title: Shanghai Composite falls another 7.6 percent
raw.description: Chinese stocks continued their collapse the day after Black Monday, taking the index below 3,000. The two-day drop exceeded 15 percent.
raw.middle_circle: After the 24 August crash, many hoped for an official backstop that would halt the decline.
raw.outer_circle: Global risk assets remained under pressure; the episode reinforced perceptions that Chinese authorities had lost control of the equity market.

raw.title: Federal Reserve holds rates, cites global risks
raw.description: The FOMC left the federal-funds target unchanged at 0–0.25 percent, citing concerns about China and emerging-market developments. Markets had assigned a roughly 50 percent chance of a hike.
raw.middle_circle: A September lift-off had been widely discussed after stronger US data earlier in the year.
raw.outer_circle: The dollar sold off and US equities rallied on the dovish surprise; emerging-market currencies recovered some ground.
raw.notes: Statement released at 14:00 ET.

raw.title: EPA issues notice of violation to Volkswagen
raw.description: The US Environmental Protection Agency publicly accused Volkswagen of installing defeat-device software in 482,000 diesel vehicles to cheat emissions tests. The allegation later expanded to 11 million vehicles worldwide.
raw.middle_circle: The scale of the cheating and the potential fines were not anticipated by equity analysts.
raw.outer_circle: Volkswagen shares plunged more than 20 percent when European markets opened on 21 September; the scandal wiped tens of billions from the company’s market capitalisation.
raw.notes: Public announcement on Friday; largest market reaction on the following Monday.

raw.title: Volkswagen CEO Martin Winterkorn resigns
raw.description: Following the emissions-scandal revelations, Volkswagen’s long-serving chief executive stepped down. The company later confirmed that 11 million vehicles worldwide contained the defeat-device software.
raw.middle_circle: Resignation had been widely expected after the share-price collapse.
raw.outer_circle: The stock continued to fall as the full global scope of the scandal became clearer and legal and recall costs were reassessed.

raw.title: Brazilian real and sovereign spreads spike amid fiscal and political crisis
raw.description: Deep recession, rising debt, political turmoil under President Rousseff, and the loss of investment-grade status drove the real to multi-year lows near 4.16 per USD. Sovereign yields and CDS spreads widened sharply as markets priced rising default risk.
raw.middle_circle: Consensus still expected a gradual fiscal adjustment and eventual recovery; a full loss of investment grade and near-4.2 real were outside the base-case path.
raw.outer_circle: FX, rates and equity markets moved in a coordinated risk-off fashion far more violently than pre-downgrade positioning had anticipated; capital outflows accelerated.
raw.notes: Brazil domestic fiscal/political catalyst. Positioning and spread widening used as proxies.

raw.title: TPP trade agreement reached
raw.description: The United States and 11 other Pacific-rim nations concluded negotiations on the Trans-Pacific Partnership, the largest regional trade deal in history, covering roughly 40 percent of global GDP.
raw.middle_circle: A deal had been expected after Congress granted Trade Promotion Authority, but final details remained uncertain.
raw.outer_circle: The announcement had a modestly positive effect on risk sentiment in Asia-Pacific markets.
raw.notes: Agreement announced after talks in Atlanta.

raw.title: Strong US payrolls report raises December hike odds
raw.description: The October employment report showed a larger-than-expected gain in non-farm payrolls. The data significantly increased market-implied probabilities of a December Federal Reserve rate increase.
raw.middle_circle: After the September hold, some investors still doubted a December move.
raw.outer_circle: The dollar and short-term Treasury yields rose; the report helped lock in the December lift-off.
raw.notes: Data released at 08:30 ET.

raw.title: Paris terrorist attacks
raw.description: Coordinated Islamist terrorist attacks at multiple locations in Paris killed 130 people. The events raised immediate security and geopolitical-risk premia across Europe.
raw.middle_circle: No prior market pricing of a large-scale attack in a major European capital.
raw.outer_circle: European equities and the euro dipped; gold and German bunds rallied as safe-haven flows increased, though the move was relatively short-lived.
raw.notes: Attacks began in the evening local time.

raw.title: OPEC fails to agree production ceiling
raw.description: OPEC ministers ended their meeting without setting a new official output target, effectively abandoning the previous 30 million-barrel-per-day ceiling. Iran indicated it would increase production once sanctions were lifted.
raw.middle_circle: Some members had hoped for a cut or at least a formal ceiling; most analysts expected no change.
raw.outer_circle: WTI fell below $40 and Brent dropped to six-year lows as the market interpreted the outcome as continued oversupply.
raw.notes: Meeting concluded Friday afternoon in Vienna.

raw.title: PBOC introduces CFETS currency basket
raw.description: China announced a new trade-weighted reference basket (CFETS) for the yuan, signalling a shift away from a de-facto dollar peg. The move was intended to increase exchange-rate flexibility.
raw.middle_circle: Markets had expected continued gradual reform but the timing added to year-end uncertainty.
raw.outer_circle: The offshore yuan weakened further and emerging-market currencies came under renewed pressure.

raw.title: Federal Reserve raises rates for first time since 2006
raw.description: The FOMC increased the federal-funds target range by 25 basis points to 0.25–0.50 percent, ending seven years of near-zero policy. The statement and projections indicated a gradual subsequent path.
raw.middle_circle: The hike itself was almost fully priced after months of communication; the debate centred on the subsequent pace.
raw.outer_circle: The dollar strengthened modestly and US equities rose; the reaction was orderly because the move had been extensively telegraphed.
raw.notes: Statement released at 14:00 ET.

raw.location_name: Kinshasa / Lubumbashi, Democratic Republic of the Congo
raw.title: Commodity-price trough and Congolese franc stress
raw.description: Prolonged weakness in copper and cobalt prices, combined with domestic political uncertainty, produced further sharp depreciation of the Congolese franc and intensified monetary financing of deficits.
raw.middle_circle: Markets expected stabilisation once Chinese demand recovered; the depth of the franc’s slide and fiscal deterioration continued to surprise.
raw.outer_circle: The currency’s depreciation and the scale of central-bank financing exceeded the gradual-adjustment paths that had been the baseline.
raw.notes: Continued Central African commodity-FX pressure. FX path used as proxy.

raw.title: PBOC sets weaker yuan fixing, fuelling devaluation fears
raw.description: The People’s Bank of China set a notably weaker daily midpoint for the yuan at the start of the year, continuing the August 2015 shift toward a more market-oriented rate. The move added to global risk-off pressure.
raw.middle_circle: Further gradual weakening was expected, but the pace at the start of the year surprised.
raw.outer_circle: The offshore yuan fell and emerging-market currencies and equities sold off in sympathy with China concerns.
raw.notes: Fixing set in the Beijing morning.

raw.title: China circuit breakers trigger first-day trading halt
raw.description: On the first trading day of 2016 and the first day of new circuit-breaker rules, the CSI 300 fell 7 percent, forcing a full-day halt after an earlier 15-minute pause at the 5 percent threshold. The Shanghai Composite closed down 6.9 percent. Weak manufacturing data and yuan weakness contributed to the sell-off.
raw.middle_circle: The new circuit breakers were expected to dampen volatility after the 2015 crash; few anticipated they would be triggered on day one.
raw.outer_circle: The mechanism accelerated selling as investors rushed to exit before a full halt; global equities sold off and the episode marked the worst start to a year for world stocks.
raw.notes: Halt occurred at 13:33 Beijing time.

raw.title: China scraps circuit breakers after second halt
raw.description: Circuit breakers were triggered again just 29 minutes after the open, prompting regulators to suspend the mechanism the same day. The Shanghai Composite fell more than 7 percent. The episode intensified global risk-off sentiment.
raw.middle_circle: After the January 4 halt, many expected authorities to adjust or defend the rules rather than abandon them immediately.
raw.outer_circle: The rapid second trigger and policy reversal increased perceptions of policy instability; global markets remained under pressure.

raw.title: Iran nuclear sanctions lifted, oil exports resume
raw.description: Implementation Day of the JCPOA occurred, lifting UN, US and EU nuclear-related sanctions on Iran. Iran immediately began increasing oil exports into an already oversupplied market.
raw.middle_circle: The timing was known but the speed and volume of additional Iranian barrels were uncertain.
raw.outer_circle: Oil prices came under further downward pressure, contributing to the slide toward 13-year lows later in January.
raw.notes: Implementation announced around this date.

raw.title: Bank of Japan adopts negative interest rates
raw.description: In a 5-4 vote the BOJ introduced a -0.1 percent rate on a portion of excess reserves, the first time Japan had gone negative. The move was a surprise after Governor Kuroda had previously downplayed the option.
raw.middle_circle: Most economists expected no change or only a modest increase in asset purchases; Kuroda had publicly dismissed negative rates.
raw.outer_circle: The yen initially weakened and Japanese equities rallied, but the yen later strengthened as the policy was seen as less effective than hoped.
raw.notes: Announcement during Tokyo morning session.

raw.title: Oil and US equities hit 2016 lows
raw.description: WTI crude traded near $26 and Brent near $27, 13-year lows, while the S&P 500 reached its year-to-date trough amid recession fears, energy-sector stress and China concerns.
raw.middle_circle: Many had expected a floor near $30; the depth of the decline surprised even bearish forecasts.
raw.outer_circle: High-yield energy bonds and equities sold off sharply; the correlation between oil and stocks reached multi-decade highs.
raw.notes: Approximate trough date based on contemporaneous reports.

raw.title: India presents 2016–17 Union Budget
raw.description: The government met its fiscal-deficit target and announced higher infrastructure and rural spending. The budget was viewed as fiscally prudent.
raw.middle_circle: Markets had been nervous ahead of the budget after a weak start to the year.
raw.outer_circle: Indian equities recovered after an initial dip as the fiscal stance was seen as credible.

raw.title: ECB cuts rates to zero and expands QE to €80bn
raw.description: The ECB lowered the main refinancing rate to 0 percent, the deposit rate to -0.40 percent, increased monthly asset purchases to €80 billion and announced TLTRO II plus corporate-bond buying. The package was larger than expected.
raw.middle_circle: Markets expected a deposit-rate cut and some QE increase, but the combination of zero refi rate, corporate QE and TLTRO was more aggressive than consensus.
raw.outer_circle: The euro initially fell then reversed after Draghi signalled that further rate cuts were unlikely; European bank shares rallied then faded.
raw.notes: Press conference began 14:30 CET.

raw.title: Panama Papers leak published
raw.description: The International Consortium of Investigative Journalists published the Panama Papers, exposing offshore holdings of politicians, celebrities and companies. The leak triggered political resignations and scrutiny of tax havens.
raw.middle_circle: The scale of the leak and the number of high-profile names were not anticipated.
raw.outer_circle: Limited immediate broad-market impact but increased political-risk premia in several emerging and European markets.
raw.notes: Publication began April 3.

raw.title: US payrolls miss slashes summer hike odds
raw.description: April non-farm payrolls rose only 160,000, well below expectations, and prior months were revised down. The report was described as an “unqualified dud.”
raw.middle_circle: A stronger print had been expected after earlier data, keeping June/July hike possibilities alive.
raw.outer_circle: The dollar and Treasury yields fell; market-implied odds of a summer rate increase collapsed.
raw.notes: Data released 08:30 ET.

raw.title: RBI Governor Raghuram Rajan announces he will not seek second term
raw.description: Rajan, widely respected by markets, said he would step down at the end of his term. The news came days before the Brexit vote.
raw.middle_circle: Many had hoped he would stay given his credibility with investors.
raw.outer_circle: Indian markets dipped modestly then recovered; the announcement added a layer of uncertainty for emerging-market assets.
raw.notes: Announcement on a Saturday.

raw.title: UK votes to leave the European Union (Brexit)
raw.description: In a referendum, 51.9 percent of voters chose to leave the EU, contrary to most polls and betting markets. Prime Minister David Cameron announced his resignation.
raw.middle_circle: Opinion polls and bookmakers had favoured Remain; markets had priced a Stay outcome.
raw.outer_circle: Sterling suffered its largest one-day drop on record, falling more than 10 percent to a 31-year low; global equities lost roughly $2 trillion and safe-haven assets rallied.
raw.notes: Results emerged overnight 23–24 June.

raw.title: UK votes to leave the European Union (Brexit referendum)
raw.description: The Leave campaign won the EU membership referendum by 51.9% to 48.1%. Markets opened to the result on 24 June, triggering the largest one-day move in sterling in modern floating-rate history and sharp equity declines, especially in domestically focused names.
raw.middle_circle: Betting markets and most polls/price action into the close of 23 June priced a high probability of Remain; a Leave victory was treated as a low-probability tail event.
raw.outer_circle: GBPUSD fell ~8–10% intraday to multi-decade lows, FTSE 100 opened –8% before recovering somewhat on overseas-earner support, and FTSE 250/housebuilders/banks were hit far harder; realised volatility and order-flow dislocation exceeded any pre-vote stress scenario.
raw.notes: Primary UK political/FX event. Pre-vote positioning and post-vote volume used as proxies.

raw.title: Failed coup attempt in Turkey
raw.description: A faction of the Turkish military attempted to overthrow President Erdogan. The attempt was defeated within hours but triggered a large-scale purge and heightened geopolitical risk.
raw.middle_circle: No prior market pricing of an imminent coup.
raw.outer_circle: The lira and Turkish assets sold off sharply; the event added to emerging-market risk premia.
raw.notes: Attempt began evening local time.

raw.title: Bank of Japan maintains policy, yen strengthens
raw.description: The BOJ kept its negative-rate and QQE framework unchanged despite market hopes for additional easing. The yen subsequently appreciated.
raw.middle_circle: After the January surprise, some had expected further action given weak inflation.
raw.outer_circle: The yen rallied and Japanese equities underperformed as the lack of extra stimulus disappointed.

raw.title: Bank of England cuts rates and relaunches QE
raw.description: In response to Brexit the BOE cut Bank Rate to a record-low 0.25 percent and announced a new £70 billion asset-purchase programme plus a Term Funding Scheme.
raw.middle_circle: A cut and some stimulus had been widely expected after the referendum.
raw.outer_circle: Sterling and gilts moved in line with expectations; the package helped stabilise UK assets after the initial Brexit shock.

raw.title: Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq hit simultaneous record highs
raw.description: All three major US indices closed at record highs on the same day for the first time since 1999, marking the recovery from the January–February rout and post-Brexit dip.
raw.middle_circle: After the early-year sell-off, few expected a return to records so quickly.
raw.outer_circle: The milestone confirmed the resilience of US equities despite global political shocks.

raw.title: Wells Fargo fake-accounts scandal revealed
raw.description: Regulators announced that Wells Fargo employees had opened millions of unauthorised accounts to meet sales targets. The bank was fined $185 million and later faced larger penalties and leadership changes.
raw.middle_circle: The scale of the misconduct was not priced into the stock.
raw.outer_circle: Wells Fargo shares fell sharply and the scandal weighed on US bank sentiment.

raw.title: US August payrolls beat expectations
raw.description: Non-farm payrolls rose 151,000 (later revised) after the weak May print, helping restore confidence in the labour market and keeping a December hike on the table.
raw.middle_circle: After the May miss, another weak report would have further delayed tightening.
raw.outer_circle: The dollar and short-term yields firmed as markets rebuilt December hike odds.
raw.notes: Approximate; August data released early September.

raw.title: Federal Reserve holds rates, splits on outlook
raw.description: The FOMC left rates unchanged. Three members dissented in favour of a hike. The statement and projections kept a December move possible.
raw.middle_circle: A September hike had been debated after stronger data; markets were split.
raw.outer_circle: The dollar and yields moved modestly; the decision kept December as the live meeting.

raw.title: Deutsche Bank capital and litigation concerns intensify
raw.description: Reports of a large potential US Department of Justice fine and capital-shortfall rumours sent Deutsche Bank shares to multi-decade lows, raising systemic-risk fears in European banking.
raw.middle_circle: The size of possible fines and the bank’s capital position had been a known risk but the timing of the intensification was unexpected.
raw.outer_circle: European bank stocks sold off and credit spreads widened; the episode added to post-Brexit banking-sector stress.
raw.notes: Concerns peaked in late September–early October.

raw.title: Sterling flash crash
raw.description: In thin Asian-hour trading GBP/USD plunged more than 6 percent in minutes to a 31-year low near 1.18 before recovering most of the move. The drop was attributed to stop-loss cascades and limited liquidity.
raw.middle_circle: No fundamental news was expected during those hours.
raw.outer_circle: The flash crash highlighted lingering post-Brexit fragility and thin liquidity in sterling.
raw.notes: Occurred around 07:07 BST / 00:07 UTC.

raw.title: India announces demonetisation of high-value notes
raw.description: Prime Minister Modi announced the sudden invalidation of ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes, withdrawing 86 percent of cash in circulation. The move was intended to combat black money and counterfeiting.
raw.middle_circle: The scale and suddenness of the cash withdrawal were not anticipated.
raw.outer_circle: Indian equities and the rupee came under pressure; cash-dependent sectors were disrupted.
raw.notes: Announcement evening of 8 November, overlapping with US election.

raw.title: Donald Trump wins US presidential election
raw.description: Republican candidate Donald Trump defeated Hillary Clinton, winning the Electoral College. Republicans also retained control of both houses of Congress.
raw.middle_circle: Polls and prediction markets had strongly favoured Clinton; a Trump victory was treated as a low-probability tail risk.
raw.outer_circle: Overnight futures plunged then reversed dramatically as markets priced fiscal stimulus, tax cuts and deregulation; the “Trump rally” began and the dollar and Treasury yields rose.
raw.notes: Results became clear overnight 8–9 November.

raw.title: OPEC agrees first production cut since 2008
raw.description: OPEC agreed to cut output by 1.2 million barrels per day to 32.5 million bpd, with Russia and other non-OPEC producers later joining. It was the cartel’s first formal cut in eight years.
raw.middle_circle: Scepticism was high after previous failed attempts; many doubted Saudi Arabia, Iran and Iraq could agree on allocations.
raw.outer_circle: Oil prices surged 8–10 percent; WTI futures recorded record volume as the market priced a faster rebalancing of inventories.
raw.notes: Deal announced Wednesday afternoon in Vienna.

raw.title: Italian constitutional referendum rejected
raw.description: Voters rejected Prime Minister Matteo Renzi’s proposed constitutional reforms. Renzi announced his resignation, raising questions about Italian political stability and the banking sector.
raw.middle_circle: Polls had pointed to a “No” vote, but markets still priced some risk of a more chaotic outcome.
raw.outer_circle: Unlike Brexit, Italian and European assets rose as investors viewed the result as already discounted and less threatening to the euro.

raw.title: Non-OPEC producers agree to join output cuts
raw.description: Following the 30 November OPEC deal, Russia and other non-OPEC producers formally agreed to cut 600,000 barrels per day, bringing the total reduction to roughly 1.8 million bpd.
raw.middle_circle: Russian participation had been signalled but the formal commitment and size remained uncertain.
raw.outer_circle: Oil prices extended their post-OPEC rally as the market priced a more credible supply reduction.
raw.notes: Follow-up meeting after the OPEC decision.

raw.title: Federal Reserve raises rates and signals faster 2017 path
raw.description: The FOMC raised the federal-funds target by 25 bp to 0.50–0.75 percent, its only hike of 2016. The median projection for 2017 hikes was raised from two to three.
raw.middle_circle: A December hike had been fully priced; the surprise was the more hawkish dots.
raw.outer_circle: The dollar strengthened and Treasury yields rose as markets priced a steeper tightening path amid expected fiscal stimulus.
raw.notes: Statement released 14:00 ET.

raw.title: Dow Jones closes above 20,000 for first time
raw.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed above the 20,000 level for the first time, a psychological milestone reached during the post-election rally.
raw.middle_circle: The level had been approached in late 2016; the break was widely anticipated.
raw.outer_circle: The milestone reinforced bullish sentiment and media coverage of the equity rally.

raw.title: Donald Trump inaugurated as 45th US President
raw.description: Donald Trump was sworn in as President, completing the transfer of power after the November 2016 election. Markets had already priced in expectations of tax cuts, deregulation and fiscal stimulus.
raw.middle_circle: The inauguration itself was fully anticipated; the focus was on whether policy delivery would match campaign rhetoric.
raw.outer_circle: Equities continued their post-election rally with limited immediate reaction; the event marked the start of the “Trump trade” implementation phase.

raw.title: Trump signs travel-ban executive order
raw.description: President Trump issued an executive order temporarily banning travel from seven Muslim-majority countries and halting refugee admissions. The move triggered protests at airports and legal challenges.
raw.middle_circle: Markets had expected pro-growth policies; an immigration restriction was viewed as potentially growth-negative and politically disruptive.
raw.outer_circle: US stocks posted their largest one-day drop of the year to that point as investors questioned whether other Trump policies would also be market-unfriendly.
raw.notes: Order signed Friday; market reaction Monday 30 January.

raw.title: Federal Reserve raises rates for first time in 2017
raw.description: The FOMC increased the federal-funds target range by 25 bp to 0.75–1.00 percent, the first of three hikes in 2017. The decision reflected a strengthening labour market and fading recession fears.
raw.middle_circle: A March hike had been widely anticipated after stronger data.
raw.outer_circle: The move was orderly; the dollar and short-term yields rose modestly as markets priced a continued gradual path.
raw.notes: Statement at 14:00 ET.

raw.title: Dutch election: mainstream parties defeat Geert Wilders
raw.description: Prime Minister Mark Rutte’s VVD party won the most seats, while the far-right PVV underperformed relative to earlier polls. The result reduced fears of a populist wave in Europe.
raw.middle_circle: Polls had shown Wilders competitive; a strong showing would have raised EU-exit and euro-break-up concerns.
raw.outer_circle: European equities and the euro rallied as political-risk premia declined.

raw.title: French presidential first-round: Macron and Le Pen advance
raw.description: Emmanuel Macron and Marine Le Pen finished first and second, setting up a run-off. Markets had feared a Le Pen–Mélenchon or other Eurosceptic pairing.
raw.middle_circle: A first-round result that put two anti-euro candidates into the run-off was the main tail risk.
raw.outer_circle: The euro and European stocks jumped as the most market-friendly pairing materialised.

raw.title: Emmanuel Macron wins French presidential run-off
raw.description: Macron defeated Marine Le Pen by a wide margin, ending the most significant Eurosceptic threat of the year. The result was widely seen as a victory for the European project.
raw.middle_circle: Polls had favoured Macron, but a Le Pen upset remained a priced risk.
raw.outer_circle: The euro strengthened further and European equities extended their rally as political risk subsided.

raw.title: Moody's downgrades China sovereign rating
raw.description: Moody’s cut China’s rating from Aa3 to A1, citing rising debt and slower reform. It was the first Moody’s downgrade of China since 1989.
raw.middle_circle: A downgrade had been discussed but the timing surprised some investors.
raw.outer_circle: The yuan and Chinese assets experienced a limited, short-lived reaction as markets focused on growth and capital controls.

raw.title: OPEC and allies extend production cuts
raw.description: OPEC, Russia and other producers agreed to extend the 1.8 million bpd output-cut agreement until March 2018. The original six-month deal had been insufficient to drain inventories.
raw.middle_circle: An extension had been signalled, but the duration and compliance details remained uncertain.
raw.outer_circle: Oil prices initially rose then later slipped as US inventories and shale output continued to weigh on the market.

raw.title: Banco Popular resolved and sold to Santander
raw.description: The Single Resolution Board declared Banco Popular failing or likely to fail; it was sold to Santander for €1 after a deposit run. It was the first use of the EU’s new bank-resolution framework.
raw.middle_circle: The speed of the resolution surprised some investors who had expected a more protracted recapitalisation.
raw.outer_circle: Spanish and European bank shares initially sold off then stabilised as the resolution was seen as orderly.
raw.notes: Resolution occurred in early June.

raw.title: UK snap election produces hung parliament
raw.description: Theresa May’s Conservative Party lost its majority, contrary to expectations of an increased mandate for Brexit negotiations. May formed a confidence-and-supply agreement with the DUP.
raw.middle_circle: Polls had pointed to a Conservative majority that would strengthen May’s negotiating position.
raw.outer_circle: Sterling fell and UK political-risk premia rose as the result weakened the government’s Brexit stance.
raw.notes: Results emerged overnight 8–9 June.

raw.title: Federal Reserve raises rates for second time in 2017
raw.description: The FOMC hiked the federal-funds range by 25 bp to 1.00–1.25 percent and provided more detail on the forthcoming balance-sheet reduction programme.
raw.middle_circle: A June hike was fully priced; attention focused on the QT announcement.
raw.outer_circle: The dollar and yields moved modestly; the balance-sheet plan was viewed as gradual and well-telegraphed.

raw.title: Draghi Sintra speech interpreted as hawkish
raw.description: ECB President Mario Draghi’s remarks at the ECB forum were read as signalling a possible tapering of QE. German 10-year yields rose more than 20 bp in subsequent days.
raw.middle_circle: Markets had expected a continued dovish stance given still-low inflation.
raw.outer_circle: Euro-area bond yields jumped and the euro strengthened as investors priced an earlier end to ultra-loose policy.

raw.title: India implements Goods and Services Tax (GST)
raw.description: India rolled out a nationwide GST, replacing a complex web of state and central taxes. The reform was intended to create a single market but caused short-term disruption.
raw.middle_circle: The implementation date was known; the operational teething problems were larger than some hoped.
raw.outer_circle: Indian equities experienced a period of consolidation as businesses adjusted to the new tax regime.

raw.title: North Korea conducts first ICBM test
raw.description: North Korea launched an intercontinental ballistic missile that analysts said could theoretically reach the US mainland. The test marked a significant escalation in the nuclear standoff.
raw.middle_circle: Further missile tests were expected but an ICBM capability was a qualitative step-up.
raw.outer_circle: Safe-haven assets rallied and Asian equities dipped; the move added to geopolitical-risk premia.

raw.title: Trump warns North Korea of 'fire and fury'
raw.description: President Trump said North Korea would face “fire and fury like the world has never seen” if it continued to threaten the United States. The rhetoric coincided with further missile activity.
raw.middle_circle: Markets had grown accustomed to verbal sparring; the escalation in language raised fears of military confrontation.
raw.outer_circle: Global equities sold off, wiping more than $1 trillion in value over the week; volatility spiked and safe havens rallied.
raw.notes: Peak market reaction mid-August.

raw.title: Hurricane Harvey makes landfall in Texas
raw.description: Hurricane Harvey struck the US Gulf Coast as a Category 4 storm, causing catastrophic flooding in Houston and shutting a large share of US refining capacity.
raw.middle_circle: The storm’s intensity and the concentration of energy infrastructure were well-known risks.
raw.outer_circle: Gasoline prices jumped and refined-product cracks widened; crude prices were mixed as demand destruction offset supply disruptions.

raw.title: Hurricane Irma strikes Caribbean and Florida
raw.description: Hurricane Irma, one of the most powerful Atlantic storms on record, caused widespread damage in the Caribbean and Florida, disrupting tourism, agriculture and energy infrastructure.
raw.middle_circle: The storm’s path and intensity were closely tracked; the economic impact was expected to be significant but regional.
raw.outer_circle: Energy prices and some insurance and tourism-related stocks reacted; broader equity markets were only briefly affected.

raw.title: Equifax announces massive data breach
raw.description: Equifax disclosed that the personal data of approximately 143 million US consumers had been compromised. The breach triggered regulatory, legal and reputational fallout.
raw.middle_circle: The scale of the breach was not anticipated.
raw.outer_circle: Equifax shares plunged more than 30 percent in the following days.

raw.title: Fed announces start of balance-sheet reduction
raw.description: The FOMC said it would begin shrinking its $4.5 trillion balance sheet in October by allowing a capped amount of Treasuries and MBS to roll off each month. Rates were left unchanged.
raw.middle_circle: The start of quantitative tightening had been well-telegraphed.
raw.outer_circle: The announcement was absorbed calmly; markets focused on the still-gradual pace of policy normalisation.

raw.title: Catalonia independence referendum
raw.description: Catalonia held a disputed independence referendum amid a police crackdown. The Spanish government declared the vote illegal. The episode raised political-risk concerns in Spain.
raw.middle_circle: A confrontation had been expected but the intensity of the police response and subsequent political crisis exceeded some forecasts.
raw.outer_circle: Spanish assets underperformed; the euro and broader European markets were only modestly affected.

raw.title: 19th Communist Party Congress concludes
raw.description: Xi Jinping was confirmed for a second term and his thought was written into the Party constitution, consolidating his authority. The congress set the tone for economic and financial policy.
raw.middle_circle: Xi’s reappointment was expected; the degree of personalisation of power was noteworthy.
raw.outer_circle: Chinese assets were relatively stable; the event reinforced policy continuity and the emphasis on financial-risk control.

raw.title: Venezuela formally enters hyperinflation
raw.description: Monthly inflation exceeded 50% (reaching ~56% in some measures), marking the technical onset of hyperinflation. The bolívar lost value at an accelerating rate as money-printing financed deficits after the oil-price collapse and production decline.
raw.middle_circle: Many external forecasts still treated high but stable double- or triple-digit inflation as the baseline; a sustained hyperinflationary spiral was viewed as avoidable with policy adjustment.
raw.outer_circle: Price increases and currency depreciation accelerated far beyond any consensus path; parallel-market premiums exploded and real money balances collapsed.
raw.notes: Defining Venezuelan monetary event. Parallel-rate and official inflation differential used as strongest proxy.

raw.title: Bank of England raises rates for first time in a decade
raw.description: The MPC increased Bank Rate by 25 bp to 0.50 percent, reversing the post-Brexit emergency cut. It was the first hike since July 2007.
raw.middle_circle: A hike had become more likely after stronger inflation and earlier hawkish comments, but was not fully priced.
raw.outer_circle: Sterling rose and gilt yields increased as markets priced a modest tightening cycle.

raw.title: Saudi Arabia launches anti-corruption purge
raw.description: Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman ordered the detention of dozens of princes, ministers and businessmen in an anti-corruption campaign. The move consolidated his power.
raw.middle_circle: A power consolidation had been expected but the scale of arrests was a surprise.
raw.outer_circle: Oil prices rose on geopolitical-risk premia; Saudi assets were mixed.

raw.title: OPEC agrees to extend cuts through 2018
raw.description: OPEC and non-OPEC producers decided to prolong the output-reduction agreement until the end of 2018, citing still-elevated inventories.
raw.middle_circle: An extension had been widely expected after the May decision.
raw.outer_circle: Oil prices held gains as the market priced a longer period of supply restraint.

raw.title: Federal Reserve raises rates for third time in 2017
raw.description: The FOMC hiked the federal-funds range by 25 bp to 1.25–1.50 percent and raised its median projection for 2018 hikes. Inflation remained below target.
raw.middle_circle: A December hike was fully priced after the September QT decision.
raw.outer_circle: The dollar firmed and the yield curve flattened as markets digested a slightly more hawkish outlook.

raw.title: US Congress passes Tax Cuts and Jobs Act
raw.description: The Senate and House approved the most significant US tax overhaul in more than 30 years, cutting the corporate rate from 35 percent to 21 percent and making other changes. President Trump signed it on 22 December.
raw.middle_circle: Passage had become more likely after earlier legislative setbacks, but the final details and timing remained uncertain.
raw.outer_circle: US equities extended their rally on expectations of higher after-tax earnings; the dollar and Treasury yields rose.
raw.notes: Signed 22 December.

raw.title: Dow Jones closes above 25,000 for first time
raw.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed above 25,000, extending the post-tax-cut rally that began in late 2017. The milestone reflected optimism about US growth and corporate earnings.
raw.middle_circle: The level had been widely anticipated after the 20,000 and 24,000 breaks.
raw.outer_circle: The move reinforced bullish sentiment at the start of the year before volatility returned in February.

raw.title: Strong US wage data sparks inflation and rate-hike fears
raw.description: Average hourly earnings rose 2.9 percent year-on-year, the strongest in years. The print raised concerns that the Fed might tighten faster than expected.
raw.middle_circle: A modest acceleration in wages had been expected; the 2.9 percent figure exceeded most forecasts.
raw.outer_circle: Treasury yields jumped and equities began a multi-day sell-off that culminated in the February 5 crash.
raw.notes: Data released Friday 2 February.

raw.title: Volmageddon: VIX spikes 116 percent, Dow drops 1,175 points
raw.description: The S&P 500 fell 4.1 percent and the Dow suffered its largest one-day point drop to that date. Inverse-VIX products collapsed, amplifying the move. The episode became known as Volmageddon.
raw.middle_circle: After years of low volatility, many investors were positioned for continued calm; a 10 percent correction was not priced as imminent.
raw.outer_circle: The VIX more than doubled in a single session; leveraged short-volatility products were wiped out and global equities sold off sharply.

raw.title: Punjab National Bank fraud scandal revealed
raw.description: A $2 billion letters-of-undertaking fraud at PNB involving Nirav Modi came to light. The scandal hit Indian banking stocks and raised governance concerns.
raw.middle_circle: The size of the fraud was not anticipated.
raw.outer_circle: Indian bank shares sold off and the episode added to emerging-market caution.

raw.title: Trump signs steel and aluminum tariffs
raw.description: President Trump ordered 25 percent tariffs on steel and 10 percent on aluminum imports. The move was the first major salvo in what became a broader trade conflict.
raw.middle_circle: Tariffs had been threatened; the breadth (all countries, later exemptions) and timing were the main uncertainties.
raw.outer_circle: Equities and the dollar initially sold off on fears of retaliation and higher input costs.

raw.title: Cambridge Analytica / Facebook data scandal breaks
raw.description: Reports revealed that Cambridge Analytica had harvested data from millions of Facebook users. The scandal triggered a sharp sell-off in Facebook and broader tech shares.
raw.middle_circle: Privacy concerns existed but the scale and political implications of the data misuse were not priced.
raw.outer_circle: Facebook shares plunged more than 15 percent over subsequent days and the FAANG complex came under pressure.
raw.notes: Story broke mid-March.

raw.title: Federal Reserve raises rates, first hike of 2018
raw.description: The FOMC increased the federal-funds target by 25 bp to 1.50–1.75 percent. New Chair Jerome Powell’s first meeting as chair was viewed as slightly hawkish.
raw.middle_circle: A March hike was fully priced; the focus was on the dots and Powell’s tone.
raw.outer_circle: The dollar initially weakened; markets digested a continued gradual path.

raw.title: US unveils $50 billion China tariff list
raw.description: The Trump administration published a list of Chinese goods targeted for 25 percent tariffs. China immediately announced retaliatory measures.
raw.middle_circle: Section 301 action had been expected; the size and composition of the list were the main unknowns.
raw.outer_circle: Equities sold off on the escalation; the yuan and Chinese stocks came under pressure.

raw.title: US withdraws from Iran nuclear deal
raw.description: President Trump announced the United States would exit the JCPOA and reimpose sanctions on Iran. The decision raised the prospect of reduced Iranian oil exports.
raw.middle_circle: Withdrawal had been threatened; the timing and the severity of secondary sanctions were uncertain.
raw.outer_circle: Oil prices rose toward the year’s highs on expected supply tightness.

raw.title: Italy forms populist Five Star–League government
raw.description: After weeks of political deadlock, the anti-establishment Five Star Movement and the League agreed to form a coalition. Markets feared a confrontation with the EU over fiscal rules.
raw.middle_circle: A technocratic or more moderate government had been hoped for; a hard-populist coalition was the tail risk.
raw.outer_circle: Italian bonds and bank shares sold off sharply; the BTP-Bund spread widened to multi-year highs.
raw.notes: Government sworn in early June.

raw.title: Trump–Kim Singapore summit
raw.description: The first-ever meeting between a sitting US president and a North Korean leader produced a joint statement on denuclearisation. Tensions had been high earlier in the year.
raw.middle_circle: A summit had been on-off; markets hoped for de-escalation but were sceptical of concrete progress.
raw.outer_circle: Risk assets rallied modestly on the reduction in immediate military-risk premia.

raw.title: Federal Reserve raises rates for second time in 2018
raw.description: The FOMC hiked 25 bp to 1.75–2.00 percent and raised its median projection for 2018 hikes. The statement was viewed as slightly hawkish.
raw.middle_circle: A June hike was fully priced; the dots were the main focus.
raw.outer_circle: The dollar strengthened and the yield curve continued to flatten.

raw.title: First US-China tariffs take effect
raw.description: The United States imposed 25 percent tariffs on $34 billion of Chinese goods; China immediately retaliated with equivalent measures. The trade war moved from threat to implementation.
raw.middle_circle: The July 6 date had been announced; markets still hoped for a last-minute deal.
raw.outer_circle: Equities and the yuan sold off as the conflict became reality.

raw.title: Bank of England raises rates to 0.75 percent
raw.description: The MPC increased Bank Rate by 25 bp, the second hike of the post-crisis period. The decision was driven by above-target inflation.
raw.middle_circle: A hike had become more likely after stronger data, but Brexit uncertainty remained a constraint.
raw.outer_circle: Sterling rose modestly; the move was largely in line with market pricing.

raw.title: Turkish lira crisis intensifies after Trump tariffs
raw.description: President Trump doubled steel and aluminum tariffs on Turkey. Combined with existing macroeconomic imbalances and a diplomatic dispute, the lira plunged as much as 18 percent in a single day.
raw.middle_circle: Turkey’s vulnerabilities were known; the additional US tariffs were an unexpected escalation.
raw.outer_circle: The lira collapsed, other emerging-market currencies sold off, and European banks with Turkish exposure fell sharply.

raw.title: Bolívar soberano redenomination (five zeros removed)
raw.description: In the midst of hyperinflation the government introduced the bolívar soberano, stripping five zeros from the previous currency. The measure failed to restore confidence; inflation and parallel-market depreciation continued at extreme rates.
raw.middle_circle: Authorities presented the redenomination as a stabilising reform that would restore the unit of account; markets were expected to give it at least temporary credibility.
raw.outer_circle: The new currency immediately traded at a large parallel discount and inflation expectations remained unanchored; the reform produced negligible lasting impact on velocity or confidence.
raw.notes: Venezuela-specific monetary reform failure. Parallel-market reaction used as proxy.

raw.title: US implements 10 percent tariffs on $200 billion of Chinese goods
raw.description: The second major tranche of US tariffs on China took effect, covering a much broader range of consumer and intermediate goods. China retaliated.
raw.middle_circle: The September date had been announced; some still hoped for a delay or reduction.
raw.outer_circle: The escalation added to growth and earnings concerns that later weighed on global equities.

raw.title: Federal Reserve raises rates for third time in 2018
raw.description: The FOMC hiked 25 bp to 2.00–2.25 percent and removed the word “accommodative” from its statement. The decision was widely expected.
raw.middle_circle: A September hike was fully priced.
raw.outer_circle: The language change was noted but the immediate market reaction was limited.

raw.title: Jamal Khashoggi murdered in Saudi consulate

raw.title: Liberation Day: Trump announces sweeping reciprocal tariffs
raw.description: From the White House Rose Garden, Trump unveiled a 10% baseline tariff on almost all imports plus higher ‘reciprocal’ rates (including 34% on China, 20% on the EU, 24% on Japan). He invoked IEEPA and called it Liberation Day. It was the largest US tariff shock in a century.
raw.middle_circle: A 10% baseline had been flagged. Country-specific rates well above forecasts, and the breadth of coverage, were the shock.
raw.outer_circle: After-hours futures collapsed. The next sessions produced a near-bear-market drawdown, a VIX spike toward 57, and a rare joint sell-off in US stocks, Treasuries and the dollar.
raw.notes: Defining market event of 2025.

raw.middle_circle: Markets had priced some tariff risk but expected more targeted or negotiable measures rather than broad duties affecting a large share of Canadian exports.
raw.outer_circle: Equity indices and CAD moved lower more sharply than pre-announcement positioning implied; investment and hiring surveys deteriorated faster than the moderate-trade-war scenarios that had been the baseline.
raw.notes: Recent Canada-US trade event. Initial price and volume reaction used; full data still evolving.

raw.title: US–Israeli strikes on Iran open the 2026 Hormuz crisis
raw.description: US and Israeli military operations against Iran began on 28 February. Iranian forces subsequently declared the Strait of Hormuz closed, trapping shipping in the Gulf and removing a large share of seaborne oil and LNG from the market. raw.notes: Exact first-strike hour is not uniformly reported; 28 February is the consensus start date of the war/crisis.
